1.1.27 — Settings, as a page

  • Settings opens in a tab. ⌘, opens Settings as a page: sections on the left, tidy cards of settings, and Find a setting (⌘F) to jump straight to one.
  • New settings. Darken pages that stay light, the page as a card, roomier tabs, letters or site icons on tabs, tabs that give when pressed, the address on the tab you're on, how soon tabs sleep, a default page zoom, floating video when you leave Pane, ask where to save, and confirm before quitting.
  • Passwords in Settings. Open your saved passwords with Touch ID, search them, copy or delete one, and turn sign-in filling on or off.
  • Updates. Choose whether updates install on their own, and send feedback straight from About.

1.1.26 — One flat window

  • Nothing in the way. The window, sidebar and page are one plain sheet, with a fine line between the sidebar and the page.
  • The page fills the window. No toolbar above it: back, forward and reload sit next to the window buttons, and ⌘L drops the address bar from the top.
  • Calmer details. Flat grey selection, smaller pinned tiles, and a plain loading line.

1.1.25 — Lighter type

  • Quieter type. Text and icons are a step lighter everywhere, in plain system type.
  • Tabs that read at a glance. The tab you're on is in ink; the rest sit back in grey.
  • A simpler sidebar. The space name is smaller, so your tabs come first.
